name: Natural Neighbor Interpolation
definition: An interpolation method that satisfies three requirements: (1) values at user-defined seed points remain unchanged, (2) interpolation between neighboring seed points is continuous and monotonic, and (3) each seed point has only local influence (occlusion). It calculates a Voronoi diagram of seed points and uses the intersection of Voronoi cells to determine weights.
summary: Natural Neighbor Interpolation creates smooth, monotonic fields by weighting seed values via Voronoi cell intersection volumes, distinguishing itself through adaptive, topology-based weighting rather than fixed distance metrics.
